title: Main Deck Ceiling and Wall Wash Lighting Conversion to Solid State Strips

issue.reason: Issue C. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

ata.title: Passenger Compartment Lighting — Ceiling and Wall Wash Lights

abstract: Conversion of the main deck ceiling and wall wash lighting from fluorescent tubes to addressable solid state strips, ending a tube supply problem and giving operators the scene control their cabin refresh programmes assume.

sections.reason: The fluorescent tube used in the original ceiling and wall wash installation was withdrawn from production in 2020 under restrictions on mercury content, and the remaining stock was forecast to run out during 2024. Independently, every operator that refreshed its cabin between 2018 and 2021 asked for scene control, which the fluorescent installation cannot provide. Tube-attributed cabin defects were also running at 11 per thousand flight hours, by a wide margin the highest single contributor to cabin snag lists.
sections.description: The fluorescent tubes and their ballasts are removed and replaced by addressable solid state strips carried on a new extrusion that clips into the existing lighting channel. The obsolete panel RO886925-91 and the obsolete galley insert D3320009917460 are deleted; the partition NY719919-92 is retained and refitted. Bolts LN983579-8C secure the extrusion at each ceiling rib position. The strips are driven from a controller in the cabin core system that already exists on all aircraft, so no new box is installed; the addressing is set at installation and stored in the cabin configuration. The ceiling and wall wash light lining at FIN 5LP and the seat track cover at FIN 55RH are removed and refitted, and the passenger compartment lighting linings at FINs 297LP and 9691LP are replaced where the extrusion changes the visible edge. Work is in zones 253, 254, 265 and 282. Revised detail is on drawings D33201135338 and D33200041146.
sections.effects: Mass reduction of 62 kg per aircraft on a full main deck installation. Electrical load falls by 3 100 VA, which is the single largest cabin load reduction available on this aircraft and is often the reason an operator embodies it. The solid state installation is not interchangeable with the fluorescent one and a deck must be converted in full, because the two cannot share a lighting channel. Cabin crew procedures change only in that scene selection becomes available on the attendant panel. Illustrated parts content, the lighting removal task and the cabin configuration loading task all require update.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only, in two variants: a straight conversion for aircraft in the original cabin layout, and a conversion service bulletin for aircraft already converted to the extended premium layout, where the channel geometry differs. Both are base tasks of about nine days and are normally combined with a cabin refresh.

type_data.balance_impact: Distributed along the cabin, CG shift below 0.02 % MAC
type_data.production_impact: No production cut-in; the last aircraft on the line already carried the solid state standard
